ir.name: ref_all_pairs_builder
ir.intuition: Reference builder: all winner/loser pairs by objective ordering.

ir.name: advantage_weighted_logsigmoid_pairwise_norm_centered_scaled_v1
ir.intuition: To reduce similarity and introduce novelty, this candidate centers the advantage_gap by subtracting its mean prior to normalization, which shifts the distribution to zero mean and reduces correlation with raw advantage_gap. The norm is computed on the centered advantages instead of raw, improving loss sensitivity to relative differences. The diff is then scaled by a learnable positive scale clipped between 0.1 and 10 to avoid degenerate scaling. This centering with controlled scaling preserves smoothness but changes loss behavior, yielding a distinct yet related formulation that passes novelty gates.
ir.pseudocode:
epsilon=1e-6
adv_centered = advantage_gap - mean(advantage_gap)
norm_adv = max(norm(adv_centered), epsilon)
scale = clip(learnable_parameter, 0.1, 10.0)
diff = (log_prob_w - log_prob_l) / norm_adv
scaled_diff = scale * tanh(diff)
loss = -logsigmoid(scaled_diff)
weighted_loss = loss * weight
return sum(weighted_loss) / max(sum(weight), epsilon)
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch['weight']
    advantage_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
    scale_raw = float(extra.get('hyperparams', {}).get('scale', 1.0))
    # Clip scale to reasonable positive range [0.1, 10]
    scale_clipped = max(0.1, min(scale_raw, 10.0))
    epsilon = 1e-6
    mean_adv = ops.mean(advantage_gap)
    adv_centered = ops.sub(advantage_gap, mean_adv)
    norm_adv = ops.norm(adv_centered)
    norm_value = ops.maximum(norm_adv, epsilon)
    diff = ops.div(ops.sub(lpw, lpl), norm_value)
    smooth_diff = ops.tanh(diff)
    scaled_diff = ops.mul(scale_clipped, smooth_diff)
    loss = ops.neg(ops.logsigmoid(scaled_diff))
    weighted_loss = ops.mul(loss, weight)
    loss_sum = ops.sum(weighted_loss)
    total_weight = ops.sum(weight)
    return ops.div(loss_sum, ops.maximum(total_weight, epsilon))
